items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: You also made some wonderful recordings with Babs Gonzales – Capitolizing, Professor Babs.

ctx.x: And Babs, of course, singing all those funny little tunes of his. So that puts it in perspective.

Okay, yeah. I’m a little hazy as to the situations and occurrences and events or anything like that. By the way, we are in an area where there was a flurry of activity. Jazz – and so-called contemporary jazz, if you will – was thriving and evolving, and there was lots of stuff going on, making it more difficult for me to delineate occurrences and meetings with people because there was a lot happening, a lot going on. It was beautiful. I didn’t mean that in a negative way, I mean that in a very positive way – as a…

and more healthy than other cycles. That was one of the ones that I like to look back on because there was so much activity. But at the same time, it makes it a little more difficult for me to pinpoint. I only have a vague recollection of this Babs Gonzales scenario. I do recall, but it's very, very vague.
